summary: This lecture introduces a series on gaining and preserving deeds that matter in the afterlife. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that Islam teaches not only how to accumulate good deeds but also how to protect and guard them from invalidation. Drawing from Quranic verses that warn against invalidating deeds and charities, Sh. Ali Mashhour establishes the foundational concept that true spiritual wealth is measured by what we retain through death and into the Day of Judgment. The lecture uses a powerful hadith from Sahih Muslim about bankruptcy on the Day of Resurrection to illustrate how good deeds can be nullified and transferred to others due to sins of transgression and oppression, making the protection of one's deeds as crucial as their accumulation.
suggested_title: Gaining and Guarding Your Deeds: Understanding True Spiritual Wealth in Islam
hadith_chapter: Hadith of Abu Hurayrah regarding the bankrupt person on the Day of Resurrection
